# dsh-cybernetics
English | 简体中文
**dsh-cybernetics is a DSH plugin that explicitly designs LLM agent orchestration as a control loop*
*: the session goal persists as an artifact of the agent's thinking; the task agent acts, the verify
agent measures, the triage agent triages, the controller advances between rounds, and the user cali
brates the outer loop through conversation — a negative-feedback loop of goal, action, measurement,
loop through conversation — a negative-feedback loop of goal, action, measurement, and calibration.
The protocol takes its name from Wiener's cybernetics: set a goal (setpoint), act, measure the devia
tion of the output from the goal, and use that deviation to correct the next action. A traditional o
ne-shot prompt is an open-loop system — the goal lives only inside the current prompt, and the burde
n of measurement falls entirely on the human; this project moves the loop into the system itself, tr
ansforming the human from "the author of prompts, one by one" into "the setter of goals and the cali
brator of the outer loop." The design rationale is described in the blog post "Cybernetics Agent — A
New Paradigm for AI Applications" (in Chinese).

- Full protocol: docs/protocol.md (Chinese)
- Evolution history: docs/CHANGELOG.md (Chinese)
## Core Concepts
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Role | Responsibility |
| **session agent** | Orchestrator (controller): recognizes user input, maintains the goal board, st

arts/collects/cancels rounds, relays results to the user; never executes tasks itself |
| **controll
er** | The inter-round state machine in `src/controller.ts`: `startRound`/`foldRound`/`runRound`, ad

vancing the subgoal round by round (task → verify → triage), maintaining the audit log |
| **task ag
ent** | Executor: an independent sub agent with no conversation history, actually executing against

the work-order brief, producing a structured delivery report |
| **verify agent** | Measuring instru
ment: accepts/rejects independently of the executor, producing a structured verdict `{met, criteria,

gaps, goalItselfQuestionable}` |
| **triage agent** | Triage: sorts the follow-up leads exposed by

the verdict into four categories — auto / defer / reject / human |
| **User** | Outer-loop calibrato
r: calibrates through conversation (goal revisions go through the session agent's `revise`), adjudic
ates human-class items, confirms completion — the controller never declares completion by itself |
**goal** is a first-class, persistent state (objective + current subgoal + full work-order brief), b
uilt on top of the dsh-goal service; since v0.2 it no longer depends on a goal.md file. The inner lo
op (task → verify → triage → subgoal correction) iterates automatically while the goal is unchanged,
with a per-round cap on consecutive iterations as a backstop; the outer loop (user ↔ session agent)
intervenes only when the goal itself is in question — a verdict with `goalItselfQuestionable=true`
forbids automatic iteration and forces a return to conversation.
## Features
### All-goals mode (`allGoalsMode`, default false)
When enabled, injects the "ALL-GOALS MODE ACTIVE" routing protocol: **every user request first creat
es a goal, then executes**; the session agent is forbidden from completing tasks in place with read
tools — even a single-file lookup or one calculation goes through the loop. Simple read-only request
s → a single `quick` round; complex analysis / write tasks → progressive multi-round `full` (async `
start` + round-by-round `collect` convergence). When the mode is off, the prompt segments and revise
behavior are exactly the same as v0.6.
### Hard gate (`hardGate`, default true — active out of the box; v0.8.10: toggleable on the settings
rd gate (`hardGate`, default true — active out of the box; v0.8.10: toggleable on the settings card)
**Hot toggle (v0.8.10).** `hardGate` is a **volatile** field: the plugins-page settings card renders
a live switch for it. Saving the toggle commits into the running instance and the plugin disposes o
r (re)installs the gate listeners (assembly strip + dispatch deny + approval relay) immediately — no
restart, no plugin reload. A hot false→true re-derives the mode from the current `gateMode` resolut
ion (explicit config wins; otherwise the structural allowlist). The other gate fields (`gateMode`/`g
atedTools`/`gateAllowlist`/`gateAllowlistExtra`/`gateApprovalRelay`) remain non-volatile config-docu
ment fields; edit those in the profile config document (saving triggers a plugin reload). Deployment
nuance: the first time this build ships, the running host still holds the pre-0.8.10 code — restart
the host once to load it; after that the toggle is hot (`lib/client.js` needs only a browser refres
e host once to load it; after that the toggle is hot (`lib/client.js` needs only a browser refresh).

## Known Limitations
1. **Host defect in settings writes**: as described in the "Plugin-page configuration" section, on t
his runtime, card saves may be rejected by the host before reaching disk (upstream #12045); workarou

nds: restart the host + hard-refresh the browser, or manual patch rows + restart.
2. **Save-semantic
s difference between volatile and non-volatile fields**: volatile fields (`allGoalsMode`, `hardGate`
since v0.8.10, `taskAgentModel`, `verifyAgentModel`, `triageAgentModel`, `roundsPerSubgoal`, `maxCo
ncurrentRounds`) take effect immediately on save without remount; non-volatile fields (`roles` since
v0.8.4, `gateMode`, `gatedTools`, `gateAllowlist*`, `gateApprovalRelay`, `toolName`, `implicitTrigg
er`) trigger a plugin-row remount on save, requiring a host reload to complete. Moreover, the host s
ettings form only serves and only accepts volatile paths — if the running host's schema is too old,

even volatile writes are rejected (a restart fixes it).
3. **`link:` installation caveats**: the cli
ent bundle's registration id must equal the package.json `name` (`@mars.liu/dsh-cybernetics`); the l
oader row id may use the short name `dsh-cybernetics`. The plugin must hang at the **top level** of
the profile's loader entries (the client scan enumerates only top-level rows); `src/` changes requir

e a host reload, `lib/` changes require a host restart + browser refresh.

es (the hard gate operating at the assembly layer rather than the execution layer, dsh-goal's focus
